Ordination biplot of a latent factor model

Source: R/ordinate.R
ordinate.Rd

Plots the site scores and series loadings of a factor model on two axes. Sites are the points on the fit's unit or time axis, labelled by their values. Series, such as the species of a jsdgam() fit, are arrows from the origin. Series that point the same way share their residual variation. Arrows are tapered when ggarrow and ggpp are installed.

Usage

ordinate(object, ...)

# S3 method for mvgam
ordinate(
  object,
  which_lvs = c(1L, 2L),
  biplot = TRUE,
  alpha = 0.5,
  rotation = c("svd", "varimax", "promax", "none"),
  label_sites = TRUE,
  traits = NULL,
  trait_arrow_scale = 1,
  ...
)

Arguments

object

A fitted mvgam or jsdgam model with at least two latent factors, set by n_lv in jsdgam() or in a trend constructor

...

Unused. Anything passed here is refused.

which_lvs

Two distinct integers: the axes to plot

biplot

Logical. TRUE draws the series loadings with the site scores. FALSE draws the site scores alone.

alpha

Number in [0, 1]: the share of each singular value given to the site scores under rotation = "svd". The loadings take the rest. 0.5 scales sites and series alike. Values near 1 spread the sites, values near 0 spread the series (Hui 2016).

rotation

The basis of the axes:

"svd"

Axes ordered by the variance of LV %*% t(Z) they explain. The first two show the leading gradients.

"varimax"

An orthogonal rotation under which each series loads on as few axes as it can. The axes then lend themselves to names.

"promax"

An oblique rotation, as varimax with correlated axes.

"none"

The identified factors themselves, centred.

Varimax and promax axes carry no variance order. Any two of them make a valid which_lvs.

label_sites

Logical. TRUE labels each site score with its unit or time value.

traits

NULL, "auto", or a data frame or matrix of series traits. "auto" takes the traits a jsdgam(traits = ...) fit stores. Each numeric trait is regressed on the plotted loadings. Its arrow points the way the trait increases. Rows match the series by rownames(traits) when those name every series and by position otherwise. Drawn only with biplot = TRUE.

trait_arrow_scale

Positive number. The longest trait arrow is trait_arrow_scale times the longest loading arrow.

Value

A ggplot object. attr(p, "rotation") holds the rotated scores and loadings, the rotation matrix rotmat (NULL for "svd" and "none"), the method and n_lv.

Details

The plot starts from the posterior medians of the identified factors and loadings. Factors with shared dynamics are identified by a rotation to lower-triangular loadings, Z_tilde and lv_trend_tilde (Heaps and Jermyn 2024). Factors with their own dynamics are identified by an ordering and orientation of Z and lv_trend. The Identification section of trend_constructors describes both. Every rotation keeps the product LV %*% t(Z) the model fitted.

The medians carry no posterior uncertainty into the plot. Axis signs are arbitrary. Two fits may need an axis flipped before they agree. compare_loadings() aligns the loadings of two fits.

A trend_map supplies the loadings as data. A rotation other than "none" replaces them and warns on every call. plot(object, type = "factors") shows the loadings the map declared.

References

Hui, F. K. C. (2016). boral: Bayesian ordination and regression analysis of multivariate abundance data in R. Methods in Ecology and Evolution, 7, 744-750. doi:10.1111/2041-210X.12514

Heaps, S. E. and Jermyn, I. H. (2024). Structured prior distributions for the covariance matrix in latent factor models. Statistics and Computing, 34, 143. doi:10.1007/s11222-024-10454-0

See also

plot.mvgam() with type = "factors" plots each factor's path. residual_cor() gives the correlations among series the factors imply. The JSDM article interprets a biplot of species loadings.

Other latent dynamics: active_factors(), compare_loadings(), fevd.mvgam(), irf.mvgam(), posterior_transition_matrix(), residual_cor(), shared_variation(), stability.mvgam()

Examples

# \dontrun{
# Gaussian responses of 10 species at 60 sites, driven by two
# latent factors
simdat <- sim_jsdgam(family = gaussian(), n_species = 10L,
                     n_sites = 60L, n_lv = 2L, seed = 3L)
mod <- jsdgam(y ~ env * series, data = simdat$data_train,
              family = gaussian(), n_lv = 2L, chains = 2, silent = 2)

# Sites as points and species loadings as arrows
ordinate(mod)


# Varimax axes, on which each species loads on as few as it can
p <- ordinate(mod, rotation = "varimax", label_sites = FALSE)
p

attr(p, "rotation")$loadings
#>              [,1]       [,2]
#> sp_1   0.60548993 -0.2315881
#> sp_2   0.68630223  0.2883360
#> sp_3   0.12719789  0.1515715
#> sp_4  -0.02685917 -0.7239206
#> sp_5  -0.52357776  0.1271335
#> sp_6  -0.11555648 -0.1464999
#> sp_7   0.46866634  0.3473488
#> sp_8  -0.07828871  0.8324566
#> sp_9  -0.42613444 -1.1481722
#> sp_10 -0.71723983  0.5033344

# Next, residual_cor(mod) gives the species correlations the
# factors imply
